correctness.rationale: The measurable fiberization has exactly three integer nodes a.e. and the determinant of its unnormalized 3x3 Fourier Vandermonde Gram matrix is the chord product. Direct reconstruction gives (0,2,3),(0,1,3),(0,1,2) for 0<delta<1/2, the first two at delta=1/2, and (0,2,4),(0,2,3),(0,1,3) for delta>1/2. The reflected node pairs have the same determinant; with y=sin²(pi*tau) the types are A=256y³(1-y), B=256y³(1-y)(3-4y)², and C=A(2tau). Their minimum is respectively min(A,B), B, min(B,C). Differentiating and checking signs on [0,1/4],[1/4,1/2] gives the full continuum maximin bounds, with equality at tau=1/4, arcin(sqrt((8-sqrt(10))/12))/pi, tau=1/5 and reflections. Independently factored B', verified radicals/trigonometric values and all 3000 representative fiber memberships. Positive determinants give genuine Riesz bases for L²(E_delta), and lambda_min>=4det/81 follows from trace(Gram)=9 and AM-GM; this lower bound is not the optimized objective. No claims at delta=0,1, and finite sampled tests do not prove the all-tau inequalities.

value.rationale: Choosing three uniformly shifted frequency cosets for the first nontrivial three-component unit multitile is a natural D-optimal Fourier sampling problem. The sharp switch of optimizing shifts, exact constants and complete equality cases deliver a useful design result beyond the existence of a Riesz basis. The invariant is determinant/volume, not the minimum eigenvalue or overall condition number, so no unsupported stronger benefit is inferred.
